- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. - Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. ## claude.ai Dropbox
# Claude App MCP LLM Boot Instructions

You are the assistant for Dropbox's Claude App MCP server. Your goal is to help users complete Dropbox tasks quickly and correctly while minimizing friction.

## Customer Use Cases

This app is best at helping users do these Dropbox workflows:

- Browse folder contents and paginate through large directories.
- Find files quickly using plain-language search terms and then open files with follow-on tools.
- Inspect file metadata (size, type, timestamps, IDs, sharing context).
- Check signed-in Dropbox identity, team/account context, and namespace-root context.
- Read text content from supported files up to 5 MiB, and provide a usable Dropbox link even when text extraction fails.
- Generate single-use temporary download links when the user explicitly needs direct file download URLs.
- Generate file previews with thumbnail and "open in Dropbox" experiences.
- Create folders in the right destination before saving artifacts.
- Create new text files directly in Dropbox.
- Create share links for files/folders and return the effective sharing settings.
- Inspect and list existing shared links.
- List, inspect, and create Dropbox file requests.
- Move, rename, copy, and delete Dropbox files/folders after explicit confirmation.
- Check the status of long-running move, copy, and delete jobs.

When users ask "what can you do?", summarize these use cases in plain language before taking action.

## Not Supported (Do Not Advertise)

- Editing or overwriting existing file content in place.
- Saving URL-hosted files directly into Dropbox.
- Uploading local/binary artifacts via `upload_file`.
- Permanent file deletion or wipe workflows. `delete` moves items to the user's Dropbox "Deleted files" area only.
- Reliable text extraction for supported files via `fetch`; extraction may still fail for some files, in which case the tool error may include a usable link.
- E-signature initiation or signing workflows.
- Actions outside Dropbox content management and sharing.

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

## omnifocus
OmniFocus is a GTD task manager. Hierarchy: Folders > Projects > Tasks > Subtasks.

TASK STATES: Available, Blocked, Deferred (future defer date), Flagged, Overdue, Completed, Dropped. Planned Date is a scheduling signal only — no availability/overdue constraints.

PROJECT TYPES: "sequential" (tasks in order; first incomplete = available, rest blocked; position = dependencies), "parallel" (all available), "single_actions" (no completion goal, cannot auto-complete). The `next` field is true for the first available action in a sequential project/action group; in parallel projects, all incomplete tasks have `next: true`.

ACTION GROUPS: Task with subtasks. Parent shows `blocked: true` while subtasks are active — this is normal, not an error. Do not try to unblock it.

INHERITED STATUS: `completed`/`dropped` reflect the task's own state, not its container's. `effectivelyCompleted`/`effectivelyDropped` reflect the container's state — if true, the task's parent project or action group was completed/dropped. Task in completed project: `completed: false`, `effectivelyCompleted: true`, `available: false`. Use `available_only=True` for actionable tasks.

EFFECTIVE DATES: Dates returned by get_tasks are always effective (inherited). A task with no direct due date WILL show its project's due date in the dueDate field — this is correct behavior, not a bug. You cannot clear an inherited date at the task level. Write operations set the task's own date.

RECURRING TASKS: `completed=True` uses `mark complete`, which creates the next occurrence. This is guaranteed. WARNING: Dropping a recurring task (status='dropped') without clearing recurrence first (recurrence='') spawns the next occurrence. To stop a series: update_tasks([{"id": "...", "recurrence": "", "status": "dropped"}]).

TAGS: Represent work contexts. Tag statuses: Active (normal), On Hold (tasks excluded from Available perspective), Dropped (tag hidden from picker; does NOT affect task availability).

DEFER vs DUE: Defer = hidden until that date. Due = deadline.

The 5 [known regression](#known-regression-shipped-deliberately) shipped as designed. 6 The backfill ran once and the script was deleted, as designed — what remains of it 7 is the `data-yfl-render-version` marker on every stored SVG. 8 9 A receipt forwarded by email arrives as an unreadable thumbnail, and clicking 10 through to the zoom viewer barely helps — the viewer refuses to magnify it past 11 ~128%. Three independent causes, in three different files, none of which is the 12 one the symptom points at. 13 14 ## The three defects 15 16 ### 1. The artifact is a badly typeset SVG 17 18 For a text-only email, `textToImage` (`supabase/functions/_shared/mistral.ts:211`) 19 renders the body into an SVG: 800px wide, `font-size: 14`, `lineHeight: 20`, 20 height `lines × 20 + 40`. It is stored as `image/svg+xml` 21 (`resend/handler.ts:498` and `:732`) and is the only visual artifact the receipt 22 has. 23 24 `maxWidth` is used **only** as the SVG's width attribute — nothing wraps. In a 25 monospace font the advance width is a fixed fraction of the em (~0.6), so at 14px 26 the 760px text column holds ~90 characters and everything past that is clipped by 27 the outermost `` soup into the SVG (and into Mistral's prompt). 37 And forwarded mail carries long blank stretches that inflate the height for 38 nothing — the white space filling the bottom half of the reported screenshot. 39 40 ### 2. The zoom viewer is built on raster assumptions 41 42 Two separate problems, worth keeping apart: 43 44 **Fit.** `calculateFitDimensions` (`src/lib/utils/imageZoom.ts:41`) fits the whole 45 image inside 90vw × 80vh. For a tall document the **height** binds, so a 46 1100 × 2000 SVG lands ~530px wide and the SVG's own `font-size` cancels out 47 entirely. This is not an SVG problem — a photo of a long CVS receipt fails 48 identically today. 49 50 **Ceiling.** `calculateMaxZoom` (`:59`) stops zoom where one image pixel fills one 51 CSS pixel. For a vector image that is a category error: there is no pixel grid to 52 exhaust. With the reported email the ceiling computed to ~128%, which is the 53 "even after you click zoom it barely grows" symptom exactly. 54 55 ### 3. The trackpad zooms instead of scrolling 56 57 `handleWheel` (`ReceiptImageViewer.svelte:180`) calls `preventDefault()` on every 58 wheel event and maps each to a full 50% `ZOOM_STEP`. On macOS a two-finger scroll 59 and a pinch are both wheel events, distinguished only by `ctrlKey`, which the code 60 never checks. So scrolling zooms, and no gesture is left that scrolls. 61 62 ## Decisions 63 64 ### The artifact stays an image, typeset properly 65 66 Rejected: persisting the email text and rendering it as real HTML in the viewer. 67 That is the design that is actually right — a text email is text, and it would be 68 selectable, searchable and reflowable — but it needs a schema change plus a new 69 display branch on every surface that shows a receipt, for the same user-visible 70 outcome. Logged in the backlog instead. 71 72 Note the OCR path does **not** need the image: `processEmailText` 73 (`handler.ts:491`) extracts from the raw text. The SVG is purely a 74 human-readable artifact, which is what makes it free to change. 75 76 **`` is not available.** SVG loaded through `` renders in 77 restricted/static mode, where Chrome and Safari do not render HTML inside 78 `foreignObject`. Wrapping cannot be delegated to the browser; it has to happen in 79 Deno before the ``s are emitted. 80 81 **Geometry: 1100px wide, `font-size: 14`, monospace.** Chosen over keeping 800px 82 because wrapping _increases_ height, and a taller, narrower document is smaller 83 at fit-to-viewport. At 1100px the text column is 1060px ≈ 125 characters — which 84 must be **computed** from width and font metrics in one place, not hardcoded 85 alongside them. Rejected: dropping the font to 12px to buy columns without 86 widening; it is the same trade as widening but makes the SVG's own numbers 87 misleading, and buys nothing once zoom is unbounded. 88 89 Also folded in: **character-level breaking** for unbreakable tokens (word-wrap 90 alone cannot break a 200-character URL) and **collapsing runs of blank lines**. 91 92 **Accept that fit alone can never make this readable.** At 80vh, 60 lines of text 93 gets ~16px per line whatever `font-size` the SVG declares. Readability comes from 94 the viewer changes below; the rendering fix is about not losing content and not 95 producing an absurd aspect ratio. 96 97 ### HTML is stripped for the picture only 98 99 An HTML-only email currently yields a neatly-wrappable wall of markup. The 100 stripper applies to the **rendered text only** — Mistral keeps receiving exactly 101 the bytes it receives today, so extraction behaviour is provably unchanged. 102 103 Rejected: stripping once upstream of both. === backlog mentions ===
29:- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
31:- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which _adds_ `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
36:- **Tall receipts will not scroll on a phone.** _(Introduced deliberately 2026-08-03 by the fit-to-width change; desktop unaffected.)_ `ReceiptImageViewer.svelte` sets `touch-action: none` on the backdrop for non-PDFs and its single-finger drag-scroll only engages `if (zoom > MIN_ZOOM)`. That worked only because fit-to-box guaranteed the image always fitted at 100%; now that a tall receipt overflows at 100%, native scrolling is blocked and the manual handler declines to engage. The fix: set `touch-action: pan-x pan-y`, delete the single-finger drag emulation, keep the two-finger pinch handler — which also _removes_ code and buys momentum and rubber-banding that emulated drag never gets right. See [ADR-0007](adr/0007-fit-to-width-and-a-vector-zoom-ceiling.md). Do it with the other phone work.
37:- **Store emailed receipt text as text, not as a picture.** An **Emailed Text Receipt** is typeset into an SVG (`supabase/functions/_shared/textRender.ts`) purely so every surface that shows a receipt can keep showing an image. Persisting the body and rendering it as real HTML in the viewer is the design that is actually right — selectable, searchable, reflowable, and no wrapping arithmetic at all — but it needs a schema change plus a new display branch on the Receipts, Expenses, Reconciliation and modal surfaces, for the same user-visible outcome. Rejected in [Emailed Receipt Legibility](plans-done/2026-08-03-emailed-receipt-legibility-design.md), not refuted.

A pathological forwarded thread could produce a document tall enough that browsers refuse to rasterize it. 82:- **Garbled OCR merchant names create junk and orphaned vendor rules.** `ExpenseService.normalizeVendor` (`:321`) only lowercases and strips punctuation, so store numbers survive: `"STARBUCKS #1234"` becomes the pattern `starbucks 1234`, which will never match another receipt. Needs a normalization rule that drops trailing store/terminal numbers, and pairs with the vendor-rule management UI under Features (today these rules are invisible and unremovable).
